nice_guideline_used: NICE NG136 (Chronic kidney disease) and NICE guideline for primary membranous nephropathy (referenced in NICE clinical knowledge summary)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: RAAS blockade to reduce proteinuria and protect renal function
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I/ARB as first‑line for proteinuric CKD

medications.purpose: Treat hyperlipidaemia of nephrotic syndrome and reduce cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises statin therapy for CKD patients with elevated LDL‑C or QRISK ≥10%

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily, titrate to effect
medications.nice_justification: NICE CKD guideline recommends diuretics for volume overload in nephrotic syndrome

medications.medication: Rituximab 1 g IV on day 0 and day 14
medications.dose: 1 g IV on day 0 and repeat 1 g on day 14 (total 2 g)
medications.purpose: Immunosuppression for high‑risk primary membranous nephropathy
medications.nice_justification: NICE clinical knowledge summary for membranous nephropathy recommends rituximab as first‑line immunosuppressive therapy in patients with persistent high proteinuria

contraindications.reason: Pregnancy, bilateral renal artery stenosis, or history of angio‑edema
contraindications.alternative: Losartan (if not contraindicated) or avoid ACE‑I/ARB

contraindications.reason: Active liver disease (ALT/AST >3× ULN) or pregnancy
contraindications.alternative: Rosuvastatin (if liver function acceptable) or defer statin until liver enzymes normal

contraindications.reason: Active severe infection, uncontrolled hepatitis B, or pregnancy
contraindications.alternative: Cyclophosphamide + prednisolone (if rituximab contraindicated and patient suitable)

Serum potassium not provided – hyperkalaemia risk with ACE‑I; check K+ before starting

Thrombotic risk not assessed – anticoagulation not prescribed pending albumin level and VTE history

Infection screening (HBV, HCV, HIV, TB) not performed – required before rituximab or cyclophosphamide
Vaccination status unknown – update pneumococcal, influenza, hepatitis B before immunosuppression
Current medication list not supplied – interaction check pending full reconciliation
treatment_summary: Start ACE‑I (ramipril) and a statin (atorvastatin) as first‑line therapy to reduce proteinuria and cardiovascular risk, add a loop diuretic (furosemide) for oedema, and plan a rituximab course for high‑risk membranous nephropathy after confirming renal function, infection status, and pregnancy. Monitoring includes eGFR, serum potassium, BP, lipids, and proteinuria; repeat assessments after each dose titration. All recommendations follow NICE NG136 and the NICE clinical knowledge summary for membranous nephropathy.
